title: Keep local builds responsive during optional registry outages
description:
Reproduced against both /Users/chazu/go/bin/mu and source commit ac5e762 using an isolated loopback registry and disposable local caches. With disk first and a read-only OCI second tier, a pure built-in shell action succeeds on a refused connection (about 0.06-0.11 s), and a warm local action hit succeeds without any registry request. A cold action lookup against an HTTP server that accepts connections but never answers remains blocked until the harness kills Mu after 3 s; its local action never creates its output.

The OCI factory leaves auth.Client.Client unset. The pinned ORAS default HTTP client has no total timeout, and optional tiered lookups wait synchronously before falling back. There is no bounded response-header wait for an accepted, silent connection.

Acceptance: builds whose required inputs/plugins/toolchains are available locally must remain responsive during optional registry outages. Bound lookup attempts including authentication/retries, and avoid paying the same outage timeout once per action. Preserve legitimate large streaming transfers rather than imposing an arbitrarily short whole-upload deadline. Cover stalled headers/bodies, refused connections, warm local hits, cold local rebuilds, write-through outages, and parent cancellation. Truly missing required artifacts must return a clear error without silently substituting another plugin/toolchain identity. Explicit push/publish operations must still report failed delivery.

The current diagnostic is an assessment, not a delivered fix. Reproduction harness: /tmp/mu-registry-outage-check.py; it constructs fresh mu.cue fixtures, a blackhole HTTP server, and a refused-port endpoint without touching the real registry or user cache.
close_reason: Bounded and quarantined optional registry outages; cached dependencies, offline mode, explicit remote errors and selected startup qualified by Linux/macOS CI 37485353093 and real PUDL integration.

title: Downstream action cache keys ignore upstream output content (stale cache hits)
description:
## Problem
When an action's input is produced by another action, mu hashes a zero placeholder instead of the real content, so a downstream action's cache key does not change when its upstream output changes. Result: stale outputs served from cache.

- internal/coordinator/resolve.go:44-56 — inputs that are `{action:id}` refs (isActionRef, resolve.go:18) and inputs whose path is produced by another planned action (`crossTargetProducers`) are stored as `cas.Digest{}` with the comment "executor resolves later".
- Nothing ever resolves them: there is no assignment to `Action.Inputs` anywhere in internal/dag/executor.go.
- internal/dag/actionkey.go:51-53 hashes `a.Inputs` as-is, so the placeholder goes into the key.
- `{action:id}` inputs also add no DependsOn edge (only crossTargetProducers does, resolve.go ~186-198), so ordering relies on the plugin remembering `depends_on`.

## Repro (confirmed 2026-11-01)
In a temp dir:
```cue
package mu
targets: [{
  target: "//a", toolchain: "shell", sources: ["in.txt"]
  config: {command: ["sh","-c","cp in.txt mid.txt"], outputs: ["mid.txt"], impure: false}
}, {
  target: "//b", toolchain: "shell", sources: ["mid.txt"], deps: ["//a"]
  config: {command: ["sh","-c","cp mid.txt out.txt"], outputs: ["out.txt"], impure: false}
}]
```
`echo one > in.txt; mu build //a //b; echo two > in.txt; mu build //a //b; cat out.txt` → prints `one` (expected `two`); second build reports "2 cached".

## What to do
1. Record, per placeholder input, where it comes from: add to dag.Action something like `InputSources map[string]InputSource{ProducerID, OutputPath string}` (OutputPath empty for `{action:id}` meaning "all declared outputs of the producer").
2. In the executor, when an action becomes ready (all deps complete) and BEFORE computing its action key / cache lookup, fill each placeholder with the real digest: the producer's recorded output digest for that path; for `{action:id}`, a digest over the producer's sorted (output path, digest) pairs. The executor already records output digests per completed action (they go into the manifest) — reuse that.
3. Make Resolve add a DependsOn edge for `{action:id}` inputs (same as it does for crossTargetProducers).
4. `mu build --plan --json` prints an `action_key` per action (computed with placeholders). For actions with upstream inputs, stop printing a misleading key: omit `action_key` and add `pending_inputs: [names]`. (`--expect-plan-sha256` and its plan digest are being deleted by mu-j11.11, so don't spend effort keeping that digest stable.)

## Acceptance
- A Go test (internal/coordinator or internal/dag) encoding the repro above fails before the fix and passes after.
- A test that `{action:id}` inputs create a DependsOn edge.

title: Target `deps:` do not order execution
description:
## Problem
A target's `deps:` list only feeds `DepInfo.Artifacts` in the plan request; it never becomes a DAG edge. Edges come only from plugin-emitted `depends_on` or an exact string match of an input path against `producerForPath`. So a dependent target runs concurrently with its dependency.

- internal/coordinator/coordinator.go:318-324 (deps → DepInfo only) and 427-431 (producerForPath keyed on raw relative strings: `./x` vs `x` misses, and action work_dir is ignored).
- docs/guide/shell.md says "Kit targets run after all their deps complete", and the root mu.cue `//lint` kit target depends on that. It is false today.

## Repro (confirmed 2026-11-01)
```cue
package mu
targets: [{
  target: "//slow", toolchain: "shell", sources: []
  config: {command: ["sh","-c","sleep 1; echo hi > s.txt"], outputs: ["s.txt"]}
}, {
  target: "//after", toolchain: "shell", sources: [], deps: ["//slow"]
  config: {command: ["sh","-c","cat s.txt"]}
}]
```
`mu build //slow //after` → `cat: s.txt: No such file or directory`, exit 1.

## What to do
1. After all targets are planned, for each target T and each dep D in T.deps: add DependsOn edges from every "root" action of T (no predecessor inside T's own subgraph) to every "leaf" action of D (no successor inside D's subgraph). Dedupe edges; keep deterministic order (sorted IDs) so plan JSON stays stable.
2. If D is not in the build set (user built only //after), it must be pulled in — check what the coordinator does today for unselected deps and keep/make it consistent (deps are built first).
3. Normalise producerForPath keys: `filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(actionWorkDirRelToProjectRoot, output))`, and look up inputs the same way.
4. Coordinate with mu-bei.1 (same files, different functions): mu-bei.1 owns input-digest filling and `{action:id}` edges; this ticket owns target-level edges and producerForPath normalisation.

## Acceptance
- Go test encoding the repro passes; a test that `./s.txt` vs `s.txt` input/output spellings link; a test with a work_dir-relative output.
- Root `mu build //lint` runs go-vet and gofmt before the kit's command.

title: Unify action environment construction; adding a sealed input drops the inherited env
description:
## Problem
internal/dag/executor.go builds the action environment in several places: `declared`/`execEnv` (~276-291), a rebuild when sealed inputs are present (~302-306), an `execEnv == nil` special case for MU_OUT (~377), and a `buildEnv` nil-inherit branch (~991-994, now dead). An impure action with no declared env inherits the host env; but as soon as it has any sealed input, execEnv is rebuilt from `a.Env` + secrets only, silently dropping the inherited env (confirmed: HOME went from /Users/chazu to empty and PATH fell back to sh's default).

## What to do
1. Write ONE function `actionEnv(a *Action, host []string, secrets map[string]string) []string` that implements the rule:
   - Pure actions: `ActionEnvironment(a.Env, false)` (fixed defaults + declared env; already hashed in the key). No host inheritance.
   - Impure actions: if `a.Env == nil`, start from host env; else declared env (current behaviour).
   - Then add `env_passthrough` vars (step 2), then sealed env-mode inputs, then MU_* vars. Secrets always last so they win.
2. Add an ActionSpec field `env_passthrough: []string` (sdk/muplugin/types.go — internal/plugin type-aliases the SDK; add to dag.Action and Resolve). At execution time copy those host variables by name. Hash the NAMES (not values) into the action key (internal/dag/actionkey.go). This is the sanctioned way for plugins to forward HOME/PATH/GOCACHE/SSH_AUTH_SOCK without baking values into the plan (consumed by ticket mu-bei.4).
3. Delete the other env-construction branches.
4. Update docs/guide/protocol.md (action field table) and docs/guide/sdk.md.

## Acceptance
- Test: impure action with nil env + one env-mode sealed input sees host HOME and the secret.
- Test: env_passthrough var reaches the action; changing its host value does NOT change the action key; adding/removing the name does.

title: Plugins bake host env into plans; shared cache never hits across machines
description:
## Problem
Several plugins copy the planning machine's environment values into each action's `env`. Env is part of the action key (internal/dag/actionkey.go ~45) and of the plan digest (cmd/mu/build.go ~206), so: the shared OCI cache configured in root mu.cue can never hit across users/machines; any $PATH change rebuilds everything; and session-specific values (SSH_AUTH_SOCK) change the key on every login session.

Offenders:
- plugins/go/plugin.bb:49-61 (`build-env`: HOME, PATH, GOCACHE, GOPATH, GOMODCACHE)
- plugins/remote-exec/plugin.bb:~196 and plugins/remote-file/plugin.bb:~205 (SSH_AUTH_SOCK etc.) plus their Go ports plugins/remote-exec/main.go, plugins/remote-file/main.go
- plugins/cowsay/plugin.bb:25 (cowsay is being deleted by another ticket — skip it)

## What to do
Depends on mu-bei.3, which adds the `env_passthrough: [names]` action field. For each offender, stop emitting the values; emit `env_passthrough` with the variable names instead. Keep deterministic, explicitly-chosen values (e.g. `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `GOFLAGS=-trimpath`) in `env`.
Grep all plugins/*/plugin.bb and plugins/*/main.go for `System/getenv`, `os.Getenv`, `os.Environ` inside plan handlers to make sure none are missed.

## Acceptance
- `mu build --plan --json //cmd/mu` output contains no absolute home paths or PATH values.
- Two plans generated with different $PATH produce the same action keys.
- `mu build //cmd/mu` still succeeds.

title: secret-gen stores an empty secret when the derivation command fails
description:
## Problem
internal/builtin/secretgen.go:87-92 builds, for the default (strip-newline) mode:
```sh
set -eu
v=$(DERIV; printf x)
```
errexit does not fire inside a command substitution and `printf x` masks the exit status, so a failing derivation produces exit 0 and an empty VALUE. With the default `create_if_absent` mode the empty secret is stored and never regenerated. Verified: `bash -c 'set -eu; v=$(false; printf x); echo survived'` prints `survived`.

## What to do
- Capture the derivation's status explicitly, e.g. `v=$(DERIV) || exit 1` followed by a single trailing-newline strip (note `$(...)` already strips ALL trailing newlines; if exact "strip exactly one newline" semantics matter, write to a temp file inside $MU_SEALED_OUT_DIR, check status, then strip one newline in shell or Go).
- Also reject an empty value: after the action runs, the sealed-output capture (or secret-gen specifically) must fail with "secret-gen: derivation produced an empty value" rather than storing "". Decide placement by reading internal/dag/executor.go captureSealedOutputs (~line 760).
- Keep the keep_newline path correct too (`set -eu; DERIV > file` is fine; add the empty check).

## Acceptance
- Tests: derivation `false` → build fails, nothing stored; derivation printing "abc\n" → stored "abc"; keep_newline → stored "abc\n"; derivation printing nothing → build fails.

## Context

It is only called when `a.Toolchain != nil` (executor.go:502), which never happens.

## What to do
1. Add ActionSpec field `toolchains: []string` — names of `from: "scratch"` toolchains the action needs (sdk/muplugin/types.go; internal/plugin aliases it). In Resolve (internal/coordinator/resolve.go:201), look each name up in the ToolchainRegistry (internal/coordinator/toolchain.go Get/ArtifactsMap: relpath → digest string), parse digests, merge into `dag.Action.Toolchain`. title: Archive extraction: symlink escape, read-through, and three inconsistent extractors
description:
## Problem
- internal/scratch/scratch.go:~345 (extractTar) creates symlinks with any target (absolute or `../`). A later entry `evil/pwned` passes the string-prefix check and is written THROUGH the symlink outside the extract dir (zip-slip). Escaping entries are silently skipped instead of rejected; hard links are silently dropped; directory symlinks make Put fail.
- scratch.go:~149 storeArtifacts uses os.Open (follows symlinks): an entry `bin/leak -> ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` puts that file's content into CAS, from where write-through or `mu cache push` can upload it.
- There are three tar extractors with different rules: scratch.extractTar (allows symlinks, skips escapes), internal/plugincatalog/extract.go (rejects links, errors on escapes), internal/coordinator/pluginresolver.go ~line 450 (uses os.Root). internal/archivelimit adds size/entry budgets with three env vars.

## What to do
1. Create one extractor package (e.g. internal/archive, folding in internal/archivelimit) that extracts tar.gz/tgz/tar.xz/txz/zip through `os.Root` (Go 1.24+), with a policy struct: `AllowSymlinks bool` (only relative, in-tree targets; resolve against the entry's dir and reject if outside), hard links rejected, any escaping entry → error (not skip). Keep the existing size/entry limits; collapse the env-var knobs to at most one (MU_ARCHIVE_MAX_BYTES) unless something documents the others.
2. Replace all three call sites with it. Scratch toolchains: AllowSymlinks=true. Plugin catalog bundles and resolver bundles: false.
3. storeArtifacts: walk with Lstat; store symlinks as links (record target in the toolchain manifest) or skip them with a warning — never read through them. Pick the option that keeps existing toolchains (go, bb) working; check whether go's tarball contains symlinks.

## Acceptance
- Tests: tar with `link -> ../outside` then `link/pwned` → error, nothing written outside; absolute symlink → error; in-tree relative symlink allowed for scratch; symlink to an outside file is not read into CAS.
- `mu scratch` still installs bb and go toolchains from root mu.cue (manual check; note result in the close message).

title: Make strict sealed routing the only mode (with a single-action auto-claim)
description:
## Problem
Two sealed-routing modes exist (internal/coordinator/coordinator.go:~362-404 "convenience", internal/coordinator/sealedrouting.go "strict").
- Convenience mode never checks an action's own sealed_inputs/sealed_outputs against the target's declarations: a plugin can claim `pass:anything` or `env:AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` that the target never declared. It also copies target inputs onto EVERY action without its own claims (including the synthetic `_transform`), over-granting; output inheritance only works for one-action plans.
- Strict mode requires each action to restate exact refs/modes, even when the target has a single action (redundant).

## What to do
1. Strict semantics everywhere: target-level sealed maps are the complete allow-list; every action claim must match a declared name, ref, and mode exactly; every declared input claimed at least once; every declared output claimed exactly once.
2. One convenience kept: if a target declares sealed maps and its plan has exactly ONE action that makes no sealed claims, mu fills that action's claims from the target maps (this covers secret-gen, simple shell targets).
3. Remove the `sealed_routing` field: any value → load error "sealed_routing was removed; strict routing is always on — delete the field". Update repo configs/tests that set it.
4. Update docs/guide/secrets.md and secret-providers.md; delete convenience-mode text (docs/guide/pudl.md is deleted by mu-fnj.1).
5. Run the strict e2e tests (internal/coordinator/strict_sealed_e2e_test.go) and convert convenience-mode tests: tests that relied on multi-action inheritance must now claim explicitly or be deleted.

## Acceptance
- Test: an action claiming an undeclared ref fails planning (previously passed in convenience mode).
- Test: single-action target with target-level maps and no action claims gets the claims and runs.

title: Concurrent mu processes lose action-cache entries (non-atomic oras index.json)
description:
## Problem
internal/cas/oci/oci.go:101 NewLocal uses oras-go v2.6.0 `content/oci`, which loads index.json into memory at open and, on every Tag (every PutActionResult), rewrites the whole file with os.WriteFile (truncate+write, not atomic). mu has no file lock anywhere. Two processes on ~/.mu/cache (parallel builds, an editor-triggered build, CI on a shared runner) each overwrite the other's index → entries silently lost (confirmed with two stores on one dir: after reopen, first entry gone). A crash mid-write leaves a truncated index.json. Open also parses every manifest (startup O(cache)); each tag is an O(n) rewrite.

## What to do
1. Store action results as one file per key: `~/.mu/cache/ac/<sha256-of-action-key>` (JSON of the action result: output name → digest, exit code, etc.), written to a temp file in the same dir + fsync + rename.
2. Blobs: keep content-addressed files (the oras blobs/sha256/<hex> layout is fine to keep reading/writing directly; writes must also be temp+rename and digest-verified before rename).
3. GetActionResult reads the per-key file; fall back to the old index for reads only during one release if cheap, otherwise accept cache misses (note in CHANGELOG).
4. Remote push (`mu cache push`) still produces OCI manifests/tags on the REMOTE: build them at push time from the per-key files (internal/cas/oci already has PutActionResult against a remote repository — reuse it).
5. `mu cache ls/inspect/size/clean` must understand the new layout (cmd/mu/cache*.go).

## Acceptance
- Test: two store instances on one dir write different action results concurrently (goroutines, many iterations); reopen sees all.
- Test: a partially written temp file is never visible as a result.

title: Verify digests on every CAS read, in one place
description:
## Problem
OCIStore.Get never checks the digest, locally (oras Fetch just opens the file) or remotely (`remoteBlobGet` says so). Verification happens only in the Tiered read-repair spool and in restoreOutputs. Toolchain unpack (internal/sandbox UnpackToolchain — also writes everything 0755 in place), and plugin bundle extraction (internal/coordinator/pluginresolver.go ~445) consume unverified bytes; bit-rot or a hostile registry passes straight through.

## What to do
- Wrap the reader returned by the store's Get in a verifying reader: hashes as it streams; on EOF, if the digest mismatches, return an error from Read (and for local blobs, delete/quarantine the corrupt file).
- Delete now-redundant per-caller checks (restoreOutputs etc.) only where the store already guarantees it.
- Sandbox UnpackToolchain: write with the mode recorded in the toolchain manifest if available instead of blanket 0755 (check what scratch records).

## Acceptance
- Test: corrupt a local blob on disk → Get's reader errors at EOF; build re-fetches/re-executes rather than using it.

title: `mu cache clean`: prune ~/.mu/plugins (incl. legacy entries) and lock against concurrent builds
description:
## Problems

## What to do
1. Plugin resolution ignores legacy 12-hex entries entirely; `mu cache clean` deletes them.
2. `mu cache clean` also removes installed plugin versions not referenced by any mu.lock in the current project (and with `--all-plugins`, every version except the newest per name). Keep `--dry-run`.
3. Add an advisory lock file (~/.mu/cache/.lock, flock via golang.org/x/sys/unix or syscall.Flock; no-op on unsupported platforms): builds take a shared lock, clean takes an exclusive lock (waits or errors with a message).

## Acceptance
- Tests for legacy entry pruning and that clean waits for/blocks on a held shared lock.

title: lint plugin: `build` must not rewrite sources; gofmt target never fails
description:
## Problems

title: Cross-target path wiring only links when the producer target is planned first
description:
## Problem
A consumer target whose input path is another target's output is wired up through `crossTargetProducers` (internal/coordinator/resolve.go; coordinator.go Plan). That map only holds producers that have **already been planned**. Targets with no `deps` relationship are planned in topological-then-alphabetical order. So if the consumer's name sorts before the producer's (e.g. `//app` consuming `//gen`'s output), the consumer is planned first. Its input is then treated as a project file, and hashing fails with "no such file", or it picks up a stale file on disk. Found while implementing mu-bei.2: its tests name the producer `//a-prod` to avoid this.

## What to do
Make wiring independent of planning order. Recommended: plan every target first, collecting all declared outputs (normalised with `projectPathKey`) into the producer map. Then resolve inputs against the full map. Then add DependsOn edges from consumers to producers, which implicitly orders them even without `deps`. Detect and report cycles (consumer↔producer) as a plan error naming both targets.
Alternative: require `deps` for cross-target path inputs, and fail with a clear error when the input path is a declared output of a target that isn't a dep. Pick the first unless it conflicts with how mu-bei.1 fills upstream digests (check internal/dag/executor.go).

## Acceptance
- Test: `//app` (consumer, no deps) reading `//gen`'s output builds correctly and runs after `//gen`.
- Test: a two-target cycle produces a plan error.

title: Root project merges examples/*/mu.cue, injecting example targets into //...
description:
## Problem
The config loader auto-merges every sub-directory mu.cue under the project root, including examples/*/mu.cue. So the root project's `//...` contains example targets: go-hello's `//hello` (renamed from `hello` by mu-fnj.5) and cowsay's `//hello:greeting` appear as root targets. `mu build //...` at the repo root would try to build examples, and example plugins and toolchains leak into the root config. Found during mu-fnj.5.

## What to do
Look at how internal/config/loader.go discovers sub-configs.
- Add a rule that a directory with its own `cue.mod/`, or one listed in a root-level `ignore: [...]` field, is a separate project and is not merged. Pick the smallest mechanism and document it in docs/guide/mu-cue.md.
- Make the examples self-contained projects under that rule.
- Also check: sub-config bare target names get the directory prefix (`//examples/go-hello/hello`), yet go-hello declares `//hello` absolute. mu-37w.6 makes sub-config targets that live outside their directory an error, so coordinate with whatever it landed.

## Acceptance
- `mu target list` at the repo root shows no examples/ targets.
- `mu build --plan //...` inside each example dir still works (examples/examples_test.go passes).
